notes: Initial intro (2025-11-04): CTO Marco Ruiz - interested in replacing in-house LLM layer; primary ask = predictable throughput for 24/7 ops.
Use-case emphasis: live agent assist + automated ticket summarization post-call. Tool-calling needs: Zendesk/Genesys actions (create/update tickets, add tags, trigger macros).
Performance target quoted by ops: 50ms token latency target p50, p95 < 250ms for agent flows; throughput: sustained 6k concurrent sessions during peak, burst to 12k for events (promo windows).
Security: must support corporate SAML SSO, KMS for key separation, audit logs retained 1 year, contract language for data residency (US-only) and SOC2 + ISO27001 required.
Quote from Maria (Head of CX Platforms): 'We cannot afford noisy fallbacks during spikes — need guaranteed reserved capacity with clear fallback tiers.'

Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit economics beat current cloud spend (current estimate $120k/mo on generic endpoints). Interested in quantization + batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.

POC scope agreed: 4-week pilot on Dedicated cluster, run 3 canonical flows (agent assist streaming, end-of-call summarization, tool-call roundtrip). Success criteria: latency SLOs met, <2% error rate on tool-calls, cost per 1k messages reduced vs existing by 30%.
Security questionnaire submitted 2026-01-22 (drive link). Legal flagged data processing addendum items — waiting on Redwood template.
Integration notes: Genesys Cloud connector planned, webhook reliability required. Must support at-least-once semantics for ticket writes.
Internal stakeholders: Marco Ruiz (CTO), Maria Velasquez (Head CX Platforms), Priya Singh (Director of Security), procurement lead Ben Park.
Existing infra: hybrid - core contact center in AWS (us-east-1) but sensitive logs archived to on-prem object store. They prefer VPC peering + private deployment of control plane.
Demo feedback 2026-01-18: LLM quality fine for summarize/assist; biggest questions were around latency p95 during burst tests and SLA language for Dedicated.
Requested artifacts: full perf profile for MPT/Redwood-verified models at sequence len 512, recommended quantization configs, sample SLA wording, and private deployment checklist.
Sales tact: emphasize reserved throughput guarantees, failover policies (regional + model-variant), and cost modeling for committed vs on-demand.
Note: procurement wants a line-item for on-prem install & support (3yr T&M).
Paraphrase from Maria: 'If you can guarantee we won't drop calls during Black Friday-type spikes, we'll expedite a 3-year commit.'
